message: Thanks. A few questions: How many people live in your household, and how many children under 18? Is anyone pregnant or is there a baby under 1, and is any child under 5? Roughly how much does the household earn from work per year before tax?
reply: Six of us. I have my son, my daughter and my son. No. Hard to say. Decent money, both of us work.

message: Could you pick the closest range for yearly household earnings from work before tax: none; $1-10,000; $10-20,000; $20-30,000; $30-40,000; $40-50,000; $50-60,000; $60-80,000; $80-100,000; $100-150,000; $150,000+? Also, does anyone get health insurance through a job, and do you rent or own?
reply: Decent money, both of us work. Yes, I'm on my company's plan. We own our house.

message: I do need a number range for this one: is the household's combined yearly pay before tax under $40,000, $40,000-$60,000, $60,000-$80,000, $80,000-$100,000, or over $100,000? A rough guess is fine.
reply: Decent money, both of us work.

summary: Virginia household of 6 with 3 children, two working adults, own home, employer health insurance. Income was never specified ("decent money"). Child tax credit is likely, since both adults work. EITC, school meals, CHIP, Medicaid and SNAP depend on income, so a caseworker should check them once income is known.
